lines.text: The task says done. But what did the agent actually run along the way?
Most tools show you the result. The path the agent took to get there stays hidden.
Agent R Q keeps the whole run, as a trajectory you can open on any task.
The Trajectory tab lists every tool call and message in the run, grouped into lanes.
And it is searchable, so you can find every bash command in a long run without scrolling.
Click any entry to see exactly what ran, and whether it was allowed or denied.
Your approvals are in the record. You can see who decided, and exactly when they decided.
Denied calls are kept too, so you also see what the agent tried, and was stopped from doing.
When the result looks odd, replay the steps, and spot the wrong turn in a minute.
And when an auditor asks what ran last Tuesday, you have the record, ready to show.
There is nothing to turn on. Every run keeps its history, from the first call to the last.
What is the strangest thing an agent ever did while you were not looking? Tell us below, then try it at Agent R Q dot com.
